analysis.title: Cross-Asset Disconnects: Rates, Gold, and Risk
key_insights: The rates bid on 10/22 appears largely driven by the continued selloff in tech and large cap growth, specifically AI winners, semis and speculative growth. Peak-to-trough drawdowns are -21%, -29% and -52% respectively.

Over the past year front-end rates traded more in line with inflation pressures such as oil prices. They have since become more correlated with equity pricing, shown by the 21d rolling correlation of 2s against AI winners and Brent crude.
The VIX remains relatively subdued and has not broken above the +2 std dev bands despite equity stress concentrated in AI, semis and speculative growth.

The author expects the subdued-VIX dynamic can broadly continue because index equity fundamentals are improving: forward EPS growth inflects higher, operating margins reach new levels, and multiples are less rich than the surface implies (SPW vs. SPX).

Japan: Nippon Life Insurance said it will consider buying more JGBs in the second half of the fiscal year, 'certainly at levels that warrant investment'. It still plans to reduce overall domestic bond exposure as it rotates into higher yielding securities. JGB 5s and 10s each rallied about 6bps.

Commodities: the lack of a bid in gold looks incongruent with yields, with 10yr USTs down about 10bps week to date. Dec-27 SOFR implied yields have shifted lower and 5y5y reals have come off their recent peaks, yet spot XAU has fallen.
The desk reads gold as still trading with risk assets (rolling 1y correlation to NDX) rather than with underlying macro fundamentals.

Largest daily movers adjusted for three-month realized vol: USDCHF +1 std dev, GBPUSD +0.7, USDSEK +0.7, JGBs -1.5 to -2 std dev across the curve, and USDPHP +1.1 std dev despite a hawkish rate hike by the BSP.

sector_views.rationale: These groups are in deep drawdowns (-21%, -29%, -52%), which the desk links to the bid in Treasuries. The note does not give a sector rating.

earnings_insights: Index-level fundamentals are described as improving: forward EPS growth inflects higher and operating margins reach new levels. No company-level figures are given.

macro_indicators.indicator: 10yr UST yield change, week to date
macro_indicators.interpretation: Yields fell as equities sold off, but gold did not rally with them.
The rally followed the Nippon Life comment about buying more JGBs, in a session that also had overnight Japan inflation data.
USDPHP still rose 1.1 std dev despite the hike.

risk_factors: Equity stress is concentrated in AI, semis and speculative growth, and it is driving cross-asset moves, including the rates rally.
Gold and oil trading with risk assets rather than macro drivers is a disconnect from the rates move.
charts_described: Figure 1 plots max drawdown across AI winners, semis and speculative growth at -21%, -29% and -52%.
Figure 2 plots the 21d rolling correlation of 2s against AI winners and Brent crude.
Figure 3 plots the VIX against its +2 std dev bands and is titled 'VIX unbothered'.
Figure 4 plots Dec-27 SOFR implied yields, 5y5y reals and spot XAU, and the rolling 1y correlation of gold to NDX.
vol_and_positioning: VIX has not broken out above its +2 std dev bands despite -21% (AI), -29% (semis) and -52% (speculative growth) drawdowns. The author expects this to broadly continue.
Gold's rolling 1y correlation to NDX shows it trading with risk assets.

tension_points.bull_case: Index fundamentals are improving: forward EPS growth inflects higher, operating margins reach new levels, and multiples are less rich than they appear (SPW vs. SPX), so the VIX can stay subdued.
tension_points.bear_case: AI winners, semis and speculative growth are down -21%, -29% and -52% from peak, and the selloff is large enough to drive a rates rally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A VIX break above its +2 std dev bands.
